message.content: Lions (family Felidae) and zebras (family Equidae) diverged from each other long before the modern families evolved. Their most recent common ancestor is the ancestor of **all placental mammals** (Eutheria). This ancestor lived roughly **70 million years ago**, during the late Paleocene, and was a small, early mammal that gave rise to the diverse lineages that eventually led to cats, horses, and many other placental species.
